response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-19
CLINICAL INDICATION: On treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer. Increasing shortness of breath over one week.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. M. Castellanos (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-09-02
TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. No difference in view or projection. The prior is displayed with higher contrast and appears mildly rotated. The current is softer and flatter and appears straight. The studies are judged comparable, but these differences limit comparison of subtle density change, hilar size and mediastinal contour.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- None

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea is central with the expected slight rightward deviation at the aortic arch. No central airway narrowing is seen at this resolution. Lung volumes are large. No focal consolidation, collapse or discrete mass in any zone. Mildly coarse markings in the right lower zone, with mildly prominent bronchovascular markings at the right base and no focal consolidation (one of two reads). Some of the right lower zone haze may be overlying soft tissue. Vascular markings reach the chest wall on both sides. The prior shows the same appearance, plus a tiny density over the right medial upper zone near the anterior first rib end that is seen on the prior only (see CAN'T DETERMINE).
- Mediastinum / hila: Aortic knuckle is prominent, consistent with an unfolded aorta, and is similar on both studies. Upper mediastinum is not widened. Right hilum is unremarkable. Left hilum is not bulky on the current study, with a small ring lucency that may be an end-on bronchus. The left hilum is fuller and denser on the prior. This left hilar change is indeterminate because the prior has higher contrast and mild rotation. Only one of the two reads reported this finding. Size change is described in words only (current appears smaller), and the left hilum needs measurement. A second finding records the left hilum as fuller and denser than the right on both studies, with similar contour and bulk (one of two reads), and attributes the prior's greater density to its higher image contrast.
- Pleura: Both costophrenic angles are sharp on both studies. No pleural line and no visible pleural thickening. On the prior the left base is partly overlapped by gas-filled bowel under the left dome.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette is at the upper limit of normal for a PA film, with sharp borders, and is similar on both studies (one of two reads). The systematic read describes the heart as not enlarged.
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or destructive rib lesion at this resolution. Degenerative change at both shoulders and in the lower cervical spine. No soft tissue gas. Fine bone detail is limited on both images.
- Other: A left-sided central venous catheter enters from the left lateral chest or axillary region and crosses the midline. Its tip projects over the right paramediastinal region at the expected level of the superior vena cava. Course and tip position are the same on both studies. No new device. The left dome is level with or slightly higher than the right on both studies, with gas-filled stomach and colon beneath it and no gas under the right dome. Gas distension under the left dome is indeterminate for interval change because the two blind reads disagreed (one read stable, one read decreased).

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: Left hilar fullness and density are greater on the prior than on the current, so the left hilum appears smaller now. This is indeterminate because of the contrast and rotation differences, and only one read reported it. Gas distension under the left dome is indeterminate because the two reads disagreed (stable versus decreased). A tiny density over the right medial upper zone is seen on the prior only (see CAN'T DETERMINE).
- Unchanged: Left-sided central venous catheter and tip position. Prominent aortic knuckle with a non-widened upper mediastinum. Coarse right lower zone markings and right base bronchovascular prominence without focal consolidation. Cardiac silhouette size. Relative height of the domes. Sharp costophrenic angles. Per the indication review, no new consolidation, pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or new lung nodule or mass is seen compared with the prior.

RECIST 1.1: not computed on radiographs

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the left hilum truly smaller on the current study than on the prior? | Reason: The prior has higher contrast and mild rotation, and both can make one hilum look larger and denser. A frontal film alone does not separate vessel from node or mass. | Recommend: CT chest with contrast, and review of the source images in PACS.
- Is the tiny density over the right medial upper zone on the prior a lung nodule or first rib costochondral calcification? | Reason: The density is well under the size at which X-ray separates a nodule from bone or a vessel end-on. It is not clearly seen on the lower-contrast current film. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. CT chest if it persists on review.
- Is there opacity behind the heart or at the left base? | Reason: The relatively high left dome and gas-filled bowel overlap the left base and retrocardiac region on a frontal film alone. | Recommend: Lateral view or CT chest.
- Is there a focal bone lesion in the ribs, shoulders or spine? | Reason: The images are low resolution and compressed, so fine bone detail is not assessable. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS.
- Is the left hilar fullness vascular (pulmonary artery) or nodal? | Reason: A frontal film alone cannot separate vessel from lymph node, and the difference in image contrast between the two studies limits judgment of subtle density change. | Recommend: Correlate with any previous cross-sectional imaging. If none is available, contrast-enhanced CT chest.
- Is the small ring lucency over the left hilum on the current study a bronchus seen end-on or a small cavitary or cystic focus? | Reason: The structure is small, overlaps hilar vessels, and is seen on a downsampled frontal image only. It is less conspicuous on the higher-contrast prior. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS. Lateral view or CT chest if it persists.
- Does the asymmetry of the breast shadows reflect previous left breast surgery, or positioning? | Reason: Soft-tissue contours are partly outside the field and faint at this resolution. The asymmetry makes the right lower zone look hazier than the left on both studies. | Recommend: Correlate with surgical history. Do not read the right lower zone haze as lung opacity without that correlation.
- What is the exact catheter tip position relative to the cavoatrial junction, and what type of line is it? | Reason: The carina and the right atrial junction are not sharply defined on these images, and the insertion site and any reservoir lie outside the field. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing. Correlate with the line insertion record.
- Are there small nodules in the retrocardiac region, at the apices or behind the diaphragm domes? | Reason: Only a single frontal view of each study is available. These areas are hidden by overlap, and small nodules cannot be separated from vessels seen end-on or from rib ends. | Recommend: Lateral view, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Is there a subtle rib, spine or shoulder lesion? | Reason: The images are low resolution and compressed, and fine bone detail such as cortex, pedicles and small lucent lesions is not reliably shown. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS on bone settings.

IMPRESSION:
1. Left hilum: fuller and denser on the prior than on the current. Whether the left hilum is truly smaller now is indeterminate because of the contrast and rotation differences. Vessel cannot be separated from node or mass on this film. Only one of the two reads reported this finding.
2. Left hilum: small ring lucency on the current study, possibly a bronchus seen end-on. A small cavitary or cystic focus is not excluded. One of two reads.
3. Right lower zone: mildly coarse markings without focal consolidation, unchanged from the prior (one of two reads).
4. Right base: mildly prominent bronchovascular markings without focal consolidation, unchanged. Some haze may be overlying soft tissue (one of two reads).
5. Heart: cardiac silhouette at the upper limit of normal for a PA film with sharp borders, similar to the prior (one of two reads).
6. In answer to the indication: no new consolidation, pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or new lung nodule or mass compared with the prior, and heart size is similar. This single frontal film does not show a cause for the breathlessness, and the left hilar question remains unresolved between the two blind reads.
7. Gas distension under the left dome is indeterminate for interval change because the two reads disagreed. Left-sided central venous catheter is unchanged, with its tip projecting over the expected superior vena cava.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- CT chest with contrast for the left hilar question (interval not specified in the findings; to be set by the attending).
- Review of the source images in PACS for the left hilum, the right medial upper zone density, the left hilar ring lucency, bone detail and the catheter tip.
- Lateral view or CT chest for the retrocardiac and left base regions and for possible small nodules hidden by overlap (interval not specified in the findings).
- Correlate with surgical history for the breast shadow asymmetry and with the line insertion record for the catheter.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
